# The Real Miami Dentists

> The Real Miami Dentists is a cosmetic dentistry education brand powered by 5 Star Smiles, a dental practice at 315 Alhambra Circle, Coral Gables, FL 33134. It explains what excellent cosmetic dentistry looks like and helps people see the difference between a white smile and a beautifully designed one.

- Practice: 5 Star Smiles
- Address: 315 Alhambra Circle, Coral Gables, FL 33134
- Phone: (305) 930-2400

- Hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM
- Google rating: 4.9 out of 5 from 394 reviews (October 2026): https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJrVsAzgy32YgR3nJl0Sxg-6Q
- Financing: flexible financing options; individualized quote at consultation
- Instagram and TikTok: @therealmiamidentists
- Treatments shown on the site: porcelain veneers (two visits), same-day resin veneers, 1-year warranty on smile designs

## Articles

### 01 · The Real Review
- [Why this smile looks natural](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/why-this-smile-looks-natural): A natural smile is built from proportion, small variations and light that passes through the teeth, not from perfect symmetry or maximum white.
- [What makes veneers look bulky](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/what-makes-veneers-look-bulky): Bulk usually comes from adding material without making room for it, so the teeth sit forward, look thick and can be harder to keep clean at the gumline.
- [Beautiful result or good lighting?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/beautiful-result-or-good-lighting): Lighting, white balance and editing can change how teeth look in a photo, so judge a smile by consistency across photos, not by one perfect shot.
- [Too white or just right?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/too-white-or-just-right): The right white fits your skin, eyes and age; teeth noticeably brighter than the whites of your eyes usually read as artificial.
- [Reading the gumline](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/reading-the-gumline): Gums frame the teeth: their health, height and symmetry can make a smile look polished or unfinished, and some gum issues need treatment before veneers.
- [Why some veneers look like dentures](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/why-some-veneers-look-like-dentures): Veneers start to look like dentures when every tooth is the same shape, shade and brightness, with no translucency, texture or variation.

### 02 · Ask a Miami Dentist
- [Do veneers ruin your teeth?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/do-veneers-ruin-your-teeth): No, but traditional veneers are permanent: a thin layer of enamel is removed, so the decision should be planned carefully with a licensed dentist.
- [Can resin look like porcelain?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/can-resin-look-like-porcelain): Composite resin can look excellent, especially on small changes, but porcelain generally resists stains and wear better and holds its polish longer.
- [How long should veneers last?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/how-long-should-veneers-last): With good care, veneers commonly last around 10 to 15 years, and porcelain generally outlasts composite resin, though habits and bite matter a lot.
- [Do veneers hurt?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/do-veneers-hurt): Getting veneers usually involves local anesthesia, so most of the procedure is not painful; some temporary sensitivity or gum soreness afterward is common.
- [Can veneers be whitened?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/can-veneers-be-whitened): No. Whitening products do not change the color of veneers, crowns or fillings, and they can dull some veneer surfaces, so plan shade before treatment.
- [Can a veneer fall off?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/can-a-veneer-fall-off): Yes, it can happen, though it is not common with well-bonded veneers; if one comes off, keep it and call your dentist rather than gluing it back.
- [Do veneers need a night guard?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/do-veneers-need-a-night-guard): Not everyone needs one, but if you grind or clench, a custom night guard is a common way to protect veneers and the teeth underneath.

### 03 · Fake or Flawless?
- [Translucency: why great teeth let light in](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/translucency): Natural teeth are slightly see-through at the edges, and veneers that block all light are the fastest way to spot cosmetic work.
- [Tooth anatomy: every tooth has a job and a shape to match](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/tooth-anatomy): Natural front teeth each have their own shape, ridges and contours, so identical rectangles in a row are a clear sign of cookie-cutter work.
- [Proportion: why size relationships matter more than size](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/proportion): Teeth look natural when their width, length and relationship to each other are in balance, not when they are simply bigger or whiter.
- [Edge design: the line your lower lip should follow](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/edge-design): The biting edges of the upper teeth should form a gentle curve that follows the lower lip, and a perfectly flat, straight edge line is a classic giveaway.
- [Gum symmetry: the frame most people forget](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/gum-symmetry): Even, gently scalloped gums frame a smile, and uneven or puffy gum lines can undermine otherwise good veneers.
- [Shade matching: white is a color, natural is a design decision](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/shade-matching): Good shade matching blends restorations with the teeth around them and with your face, while a shade that is too white or too flat stands out instantly.
- [Surface texture: the detail you feel before you see](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/surface-texture): Natural enamel has fine ridges and a soft sheen, and restorations that are glassy-smooth or dull stand out even when the color is right.

### 04 · Miami Smile Files
- [Smiles, confidence, identity and personal style](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/smiles-confidence-identity-and-personal-style): Miami Smile Files is about the people behind the smiles: how a smile carries confidence, identity and style, and why the best work looks like it was always yours.
- [Confidence: what a smile changes, and what it doesn't](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/confidence): Research links how people feel about their teeth with how freely they smile, but cosmetic work supports confidence rather than creating it.
- [Identity: a new smile should still look like you](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/identity): Your smile is part of how people recognize you, so good cosmetic work refines it instead of replacing it with someone else's.
- [Personal style: your smile is part of the look](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/personal-style): Clothes, hair and makeup change with the season, but a smile is a long-term choice, so it should suit your style without chasing it.
- [On camera: what lenses, lights and screens do to a smile](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/on-camera): Cameras exaggerate some flaws and flatten others, so a smile that looks great on camera is designed for real light first and photos second.
- [Miami culture: a city that smiles out loud](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/miami-culture): Miami's mix of cultures, sun and social life puts smiles on display, and well-planned work reflects that diversity rather than one ideal.

### 05 · The Redo Room
- [Focus on the solution. Protect the patient’s dignity.](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/focus-on-the-solution-protect-the-patients-dignity): The Redo Room shows how dental work that did not turn out right can be corrected, without shaming the patient or the dentist who came before.
- [Replacing bulky veneers: how thick work gets slimmed down](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/replacing-bulky-veneers): Bulky veneers can often be redone with thinner, better-shaped ones, but it starts with a careful exam of the teeth and gums underneath.
- [Fixing mismatched shades: bringing one smile back to one color](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/fixing-mismatched-shades): When restorations and natural teeth no longer match, the fix depends on what changed and what can still change color.
- [Correcting a flat smile line: restoring the curve](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/correcting-a-flat-smile-line): A flat smile line can make a smile look older or artificial, and correcting it means re-planning the edges, the gums and sometimes the bite together.
- [Repairing chipped bonding: when to patch and when to redo](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/repairing-chipped-bonding): Small chips in composite bonding can often be repaired in a single visit, while widespread staining, wear or decay may call for replacement.

### 06 · The Real Answer
- [The Real Answer, in 15 to 35 seconds](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/reels-15-to-35-seconds): The Real Answer is built for short video: one trending dental question, one straight answer, in a 15 to 35 second Reel. Here is how the format works.
- [Overseas veneer deals: the price is not the whole bill](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/overseas-veneer-deals): A cheaper veneer trip can work out, but you are buying irreversible work with thinner oversight and follow-up care an ocean away.
- [Charcoal toothpaste: dark paste, no proof](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/charcoal-toothpaste): There is no good evidence charcoal toothpaste whitens teeth or is safe for long-term use, and abrasive scrubbing can make teeth look more yellow.
- [DIY whitening trends: what the videos leave out](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/diy-whitening-trends): Most viral whitening hacks either do nothing or wear down enamel; real whitening uses peroxide, ideally chosen with a dentist.
- [Bonding or veneers? Start with the smallest change that works](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/bonding-or-veneers): Bonding suits small, reversible fixes; porcelain veneers suit bigger, longer-lasting changes but require removing enamel.
- [Filters vs real results: your teeth are not a preset](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/filters-vs-real-results): Filtered smile photos set a standard real teeth cannot meet; judge results in natural light and with a try-in on your own teeth.

### 07 · Before You Touch Your Teeth
- [Before You Touch Your Teeth: the checklist in carousels and stories](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/carousels-and-stories): Before You Touch Your Teeth runs as swipeable carousels and Stories on social media. This is the full checklist in one place.
- [Is the dentist licensed in Florida? Check it yourself in two minutes](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/is-the-dentist-licensed-in-florida): The Florida Department of Health runs a free online license lookup; use it to confirm any dentist's license before cosmetic work.
- [Will I see a preview first? You should, on your own teeth](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/will-i-see-a-preview-first): For veneers and smile design, ask for a physical mock-up on your unprepared teeth so you can judge the result before anything is removed.
- [How much enamel comes off? Ask for the number](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/how-much-enamel-comes-off): Traditional porcelain veneers usually remove a fraction of a millimeter of enamel from the front of the tooth, and that enamel does not grow back.
- [What does the warranty cover? Get it in writing](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/what-does-the-warranty-cover): Cosmetic warranties vary widely; ask exactly what is covered, for how long, under what conditions, and what is excluded, and get it in writing.
- [Who makes the veneers? Ask for the lab and the material](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/who-makes-the-veneers): Porcelain veneers are usually made by a dental lab technician; ask which lab, where it is, and what material it uses.
- [Is there a written treatment plan? Do not start without one](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/is-there-a-written-treatment-plan): Before cosmetic work, ask for a written plan listing each tooth, each procedure, the materials, the sequence and the alternatives you discussed.

### 08 · Dental Tech & AI
- [AI that reads your X-rays: what it flags, and what it doesn't decide](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/ai-that-reads-your-x-rays): FDA-cleared software can now mark suspected decay and other findings on dental X-rays. It highlights; your dentist still diagnoses.
- [AI that checks the X-ray before anyone reads it](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/ai-checks-on-x-ray-quality): Overjet says the FDA has cleared its IRIS software to flag X-ray quality problems right after capture, aiming to catch a bad image before you leave the chair.
- [Digital smile previews: see the plan before anyone touches a tooth](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/digital-smile-previews): Smile design software and printed or milled mock-ups let you preview veneers on your own face, and try them in your mouth, before treatment begins.
- [Scans instead of impressions: goodbye to the putty tray](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/scans-instead-of-impressions): Intraoral scanners build a 3D model of your teeth with a small wand, and for many single-tooth and cosmetic cases they can replace impression putty.
- [Same-day 3D-printed veneers: fast is real, but resin is not porcelain](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/same-day-3d-printed-veneers): Chairside printers can make resin veneers in a single visit. The speed is real; long-term evidence is thin, and printed resin still differs from porcelain.
- [Dental MRI arrives in the US: imaging without radiation](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/dental-mri-arrives-in-the-us): Dentsply Sirona and Siemens Healthineers announced FDA clearance for a dental-dedicated MRI in March 2026: soft-tissue detail without ionizing radiation.
- [Should you trust an AI diagnosis? Trust the dentist who uses it well](https://therealmiamidentists.com/articles/should-you-trust-an-ai-diagnosis): Dental AI works best as a second reader. Your dentist makes the diagnosis and stays responsible for it, and you are entitled to ask how the tool is used.

## FAQ

- [Veneers vs teeth whitening: which should I choose?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Whitening lightens your natural enamel; veneers replace the visible front surface of the tooth.
- [Which cosmetic procedures work for a full smile redesign in Coral Gables?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): A full smile redesign usually combines treatments planned together: porcelain veneers for shape and color, gum contouring to balance the gumline, whitening for natural teeth that stay visible, and sometimes bonding or crowns for worn or damaged teeth.
- [Can I fix my gum contour and alignment without braces?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Often, yes.
- [What is the best approach for a natural-looking smile?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Design the smile around your face, not a shade tab.
- [How do I evaluate cosmetic dentistry before-and-after photos?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Compare like with like: the same lighting, angle, distance and lip position in both shots.
- [Why isn't my teeth whitening making my teeth bright enough?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Several things limit whitening.
- [What noninvasive cosmetic dentistry options are there?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Professional whitening, composite bonding, clear aligners and minimal-preparation or no-preparation veneers all change a smile with little or no removal of healthy tooth structure.
- [What does a smile makeover cost upfront in Miami, and is financing available?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Cost depends on how many teeth are treated, the material (porcelain or resin), whether gum contouring or other work is needed, and how complex the case is, so reputable practices quote individually after an exam rather than from a price list.
- [Who should I hire for a full smile design?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Choose a cosmetic dentist who does full smile designs routinely, not occasionally.
- [What happens during a cosmetic dentistry consultation?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Expect a conversation about what you like and dislike in your smile, an exam of your teeth, gums and bite, and photos or digital scans.
- [How do I check that a Miami dentist is licensed?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Every dentist practicing in Florida must hold an active license from the Florida Board of Dentistry.
- [Is a cosmetic dentist a dental specialist?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): No.
- [How long do porcelain and resin veneers last?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): With good care, porcelain veneers commonly last 10 to 15 years or longer, and resin (composite) veneers typically last around 5 to 7 years.
- [Are veneers reversible?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Traditional porcelain veneers usually involve removing a thin layer of enamel, often around half a millimeter, so they are considered permanent: that tooth will always need a covering.
- [Should I travel abroad for cheaper veneers?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Some people get good results, but the risks are real.
- [How do I take care of veneers?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Care for veneers much like natural teeth: brush twice a day with a non-abrasive toothpaste, floss daily and keep regular cleaning appointments.
- [Does dental insurance cover veneers?](https://therealmiamidentists.com/#faq): Usually not.
